MetodologIA · Class 01 · Practice workbook

Document a pilot the team can review and repeat.

An experiment without authorized sources, owners or exit criteria does not create organizational learning.

Journey outcomeA purposeful source base, reviewed evidence, a sufficiency verdict and an AI role chosen with judgment.
View promptsView masterclass

The workbook turns the session into a shared record of preparation, execution, evidence and transfer.

Define the workflow, owner, allowed sources, human control and metric before execution.

Keep inputs, citations, decisions, exceptions and outcomes so another person can audit the pilot.

00 · How to use it

How to use it

Start by preparing a real case. In class you complete five guided steps. Then you can deepen the work, consolidate evidence and, optionally, turn reviewed research into a skill.

Usage conditions

For sheets 2 and 3, a paid ChatGPT or Claude plan may provide more continuity and capacity, but it does not guarantee better results. Always verify current official conditions.

Preparation · one input, three moves

Prepare your case

Start with free-form dictation. Reuse the same field as a handoff space: after prompt 1 paste the confirmed version; after prompt 2 paste the agreed brief; then run the preplan. Nothing is retained after reload.

01

Dump, clean and confirm a session dictation

Prompt 01
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

We need to order the dictation of a [TEAM] session about [PROCESS] before the workshop. I paste it here: {{BRAIN_DUMP}}. Work only with that dictation and the attachments actually received: do not invent sentences, data or attachments nobody dictated. Strip repetition conservatively, without erasing intent, nuance or the vocabulary specific to [PROCESS]. Attribute every idea to whoever said it; if the dictation does not support that, mark it unattributed instead of guessing. If the dictation is inaudible or unintelligible, ask for the recording again instead of cleaning it. If two voices in [TEAM] contradict each other, keep both and mark the contradiction; do not resolve it. Separate stated facts, your interpretations and gaps. Confirm the understanding in five points at most and declare what you could not interpret. List the pending decisions of the team with a proposed owner and, for each one, the operational risk of moving on without deciding it. Then ask at most three strategic questions, one per turn and waiting for the answer, aimed at whoever can answer them. Close with the clean version and what changed in the understanding, in a format ready for review by someone who was not in the session. If the dictation already arrives clean and attributed, say so and return only the gaps. Do not propose a solution or a tool yet.

Level 2Structured

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every idea in the summary carries a declared author or the explicit unattributed mark
  • Each pending decision lists a proposed owner and the operational risk of leaving it open
  • Someone who was not in the session can read the close and mark each point right or corrected

Edge cases

  • A single voice in the dictation: attribution is declared trivial and no participants are invented
  • Contradiction between two voices: it is kept and flagged, never averaged

Trade-offs

  • Attributing voices lengthens the summary in exchange for decisions that have an owner
  • This turn gives up the cleaning-level control the individual cell exposes: with several voices, aggressive compression erases authorship, so the level stays pinned to conservative. The original definition of done promised the person recognizes their intent and "discovers possibilities": here it is replaced by facts of the turn — ideas attributed or marked, five points confirmed, decisions with owner and risk — because discovery is neither produced nor verified by the prompt

Assumptions

  • The dictation comes from a real session and no record beyond the pasted text is available

Limits

  • It leaves the material confirmed and reviewable; it neither classifies the intent nor writes the assignment
  • It approves no decision and replaces nobody who must take one: it only names the proposed owner
02

Define the learning assignment for a team

Prompt 02
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

Turn what [TEAM] already confirmed into an assignment before talking about tools. The target outcome is [OUTCOME] and it will be applied within [PROCESS]. I paste the material here: {{BRAIN_DUMP}}. Classify the main intent among study, learn, create, decide, prepare a conversation, configure an advisor or configure a coach; if two appear, declare as main the one that blocks the other; if none fits, say so and propose the closest. Write the sentence "We want to understand or produce [OUTCOME] so we can decide within [PROCESS]". Define audience, deadline, the current level of the team and constraints from what was dictated; whatever is unsaid, ask for it: do not invent sources, deadlines or constraints. Set a minimum evidence that is observable and comparable across members of [TEAM]: something a reviewer can call done or not done without having been in the session. Name the role that takes the final decision and the operational risk of leaving it ownerless. State what is out of scope. Return a one-page brief with those sections, ready for review, and ask for confirmation section by section. If anyone asks to jump to tools, declare it out: the assignment comes first.

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The brief carries every requested section and each one comes back marked as confirmed or corrected
  • A reviewer who was not in the session can call the minimum evidence done or not done
  • The final decision appears with a named role, not with a vague collective

Edge cases

  • Decision with no assigned role: it is requested before closing, because without an owner the assignment is not executable
  • Process constraints never dictated: they are requested instead of completed

Trade-offs

  • Agreeing the assignment costs one review round in exchange for not spending learning hours on an ambiguous target
  • This turn drops the tailored individual evidence the personal cell allows: here the evidence must be comparable across members, and that comparability is paid for with less fit to each person’s level. The original definition of done promised the assignment "enables a later decision about the needed Notebook and sources": that happens in a later turn, so what is checked here is the confirmed sections, the named role and evidence a reviewer can declare

Assumptions

  • A role with authority for the final decision exists, and so does a process where the learning will be applied

Limits

  • It produces the agreed assignment; it neither picks a tool nor selects material
  • It informs the decision, it neither approves nor replaces it
03

Turn it into a NotebookLM preplan for a team

Prompt 03
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

We are preparing a NotebookLM preplan for [TEAM] before the workshop. The confirmed assignment is [CONFIRMED ASSIGNMENT] and the candidate material is [AVAILABLE MATERIAL]. I paste it here: {{BRAIN_DUMP}}. Classify the case among study, learn something new, create source-grounded content, prepare a decision or meeting, configure an advisor, configure a coach, or turn research into a skill; if none fits, say so and propose the closest. Write "This Notebook exists to…" derived from [CONFIRMED ASSIGNMENT], and define the audience inside [TEAM], the observable outcome and who takes the final decision. Split [AVAILABLE MATERIAL] into loadable, gaps to research and excluded by privacy or rights; treat exclusion as a policy of the team and cite the reason per item, not the judgement of whoever pasted the material. If everything ends up excluded, stop, declare coverage_gap and name the operational risk of starting without licensed material. Recommend a source-grounded role —teacher, advisor or coach— and its explicit boundary. Deliver the plan mapped to the five workshop steps: build, audit, research, decide sufficiency and activate the role, ready for review by someone who did not write it. Close with the first evidence and who reviews it. Do not invent sources, attachments or NotebookLM capabilities.

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every candidate item sits in a single list and every exclusion cites the policy behind it
  • The recommended role comes with a boundary sentence saying what it will not do
  • Someone who did not write the preplan can read it and say whether each piece is there or missing

Edge cases

  • Material with doubtful rights: it is excluded and the doubt declared, instead of assuming permission
  • Zero licensed material: the preplan stops with coverage_gap and a declared operational risk

Trade-offs

  • Applying exclusion as policy slows the start in exchange for never loading material that has to be pulled back
  • This turn gives up the case-by-case judgement of whoever pasted the material, which the individual cell keeps: here the reason must cite team policy so a third party can check the exclusion. The original definition of done promised the preplan "lets the person open NotebookLM and begin": that happens outside the turn, so what is checked here are the delivered pieces — material lists with the policy cited, role with boundary, five steps, first evidence and its reviewer

Assumptions

  • An applicable privacy and rights policy exists, and so does a role with authority for the final decision

Limits

  • It preplans; it neither creates the Notebook, uploads material, nor runs the workshop steps
  • It promises no tool capability beyond what is documented, and it does not approve the use of the material: it leaves it reviewable

Before you continue

Prepare for the workshop

01

Prerequisites

  • Google account with access to NotebookLM.
  • Updated desktop browser; phone as a secondary device.
  • Basic familiarity with AI chat: write, iterate and review.
  • Willingness to learn a new way of working.
02

Inputs

  • A real topic, decision or problem.
  • Three to eight sources you are allowed to use.
  • The audience and outcome you want to produce.
  • A criterion for deciding when the base is sufficient.
03

Working boundaries

  • Do not upload personal, confidential or restricted data.
  • Citations support review; they do not guarantee accuracy.
  • The workbook does not save or send answers.
  • The final decision and risk remain human.

W00 · Total duration 60–120 min · Requirement: Google account, browser and real topic. Privacy: do not upload personal or confidential data. This document does not save or send your answers; print or save locally only if you choose. You decide; NotebookLM organizes and cites; the facilitator guides.
NotebookLM can answer from selected sources and show citations; these aids do not guarantee accuracy. Inspect the source and keep human judgment. Deep Research requires users to be 18 or older and availability can vary by account, plan and surface; check official help.

01–03 · Workbook

Three practice routes.

01 · In session

Five steps

Define purpose, review sources and decide when evidence is sufficient.

1

A first shared base for the team

Expected evidence: a decision and cited evidence.

Inputs: topic, purpose and context · Action: run and review · Output: cited response · Check: inspect the source · Next: decide whether to continue.

Prompt 1
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

Step 1 of the workshop: the team needs a verifiable knowledge base about [TOPIC] and nothing is loaded yet. [TEAM] will consume it within [PROCESS] before [TEAM DECISION]. Define a splittable scope and questions; explain the essentials and what changed since [CUTOFF DATE]; prioritize primary sources with internal usage rights; include tensions and evidence limits; separate facts, interpretations and uncertainty, tagging every uncertain line as "uncertain: X is missing"; recommend each source with title, author, date, link, reason and an accountable owner. Do not stop at scoping and do not close on a sufficiency rule: deliver a cited report ready for review, importable as the first shared source and auditable in the next step. Without primary sources with clear rights, deliver the shorter report, record the operational risk and list the gaps. Do not invent sources, citations or usage rights.
2Level 2 · StructuredMakes inputs, options, flow and expected result explicit.
Level 2Structured

Makes inputs, options, flow and expected result explicit.

3Level 3 · SpecifiedAdds contract, boundaries, verification and definition of done.

Record topic, team decision, consuming team, process and cutoff date2. Define a splittable scope and frame the essential questions3. Explain the essentials and what changed since the cutoff date4. Prioritize primary sources with internal usage rights, reason and owner5. Separate facts, interpretations and uncertainty and tag every uncertain line6. Deliver the cited report ready for review and importable as a shared source# Expected output- Cited report with splittable scope, essentials, tensions and limits- Primary sources with usage rights, reason and an accountable owner- Operational risk and gaps recorded for the audit step
Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The scope is splittable across members and every block has someone it can be assigned to
  • Every source carries title, author, date, link, reason, internal usage rights and an owner; without rights it stays out
  • Every uncertain line carries the tag "uncertain: X is missing", readable by a reviewer who was not in the workshop

Edge cases

  • No primary sources with clear rights: shorter report, operational risk recorded and gaps listed
  • Team decision without a defined owner: the prompt asks before scoping

Trade-offs

  • Checking usage rights and naming an owner adds friction in exchange for a shareable base with no internal legal risk
  • This cell replaces the individual context and audience of the base text with a consuming team and a process: it loses the calibration to a single reader and gains a splittable report; no other step 1 instruction is lost

Assumptions

  • A team will consume the base and a process exists where the result applies
  • The skeleton of scope, facts versus interpretations and primary sources with a reason is inherited from the standalone variant 01; here it ends in a shareable report, not in a sufficiency rule
  • If prior preparation happened, the preplan orients the scope; it brings no loaded sources: the Notebook is still empty when step 1 starts

Limits

  • It produces the first shared base, not an approved base: it informs the review, it does not replace it
  • It does not audit or rank the gaps of what it delivers: that belongs to W02

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The summary fits in eight lines and the table carries all six columns, owner included
  • Every finding carries the citation of the selected source that holds it
  • "What the team can claim today" is a list where every line carries its citation: without one the line stays out, and that rule replaces the adjective "honest"

Edge cases

  • Single-source base: the prompt forces a bias audit before any other dimension
  • Findings that contradict across sources: they are typed as a tension in the table instead of averaged

Trade-offs

  • A fixed format and an owner per action in exchange for comparability across process reviews
  • This cell swaps the individual audience of the base text for the agreed purpose and the process, and ranks gaps by operational risk instead of personal blocking: it loses the reading tailored to one reader and gains an actionable table; no other step 2 instruction is lost

Assumptions

  • The shared base was built in step 1 and the team agreed on a purpose
  • The core dimensions are inherited from the standalone audit 05; here they do not close in a verdict

Limits

  • It does not write the assistant instruction or its starter prompts
  • It does not decide sufficiency or approve external use: that belongs to W04 and to the owner review

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The brief carries objective, in and out of scope, minimum evidence and acceptance criteria: it is reviewed as a checklist
  • Another team member can run it reading the brief alone, without asking the author for context
  • The chosen gap carries the operational risk it leaves open in the process, named

Edge cases

  • No prior diagnosis: the prompt asks for the audit instead of inventing gaps
  • Risks tied across gaps: it asks the accountable owner instead of deciding for the process

Trade-offs

  • A self-explaining brief costs more text in exchange for not depending on whoever attended the workshop
  • This cell changes the impact test: where the persona cell picks the gap blocking most claimable lines, here it picks the one with the highest operational risk in the process, and the personal case context is replaced by the process; no other step 3 instruction is lost

Assumptions

  • A team diagnosis exists with open gaps and an accountable owner to ask
  • The brief anatomy is inherited from the standalone research 03; there the research runs, here it is only commissioned
  • Deep Research is available for the team accounts: availability varies by plan and age, and the prompt does not promise it

Limits

  • It generates the brief, it does not run the research or approve its result
  • It does not re-audit the shared base or decide sufficiency: that belongs to W02 and W04

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The comparison walks the four points of the previous audit: gap, claims, tensions and residual risk
  • The verdict never travels alone: sufficient carries limits readable by someone who was not in the workshop, and repeat carries the next prompt
  • Sufficient has an operational definition — no open gap blocks the process — checkable against the gap list

Edge cases

  • New sources that contradict the shared base: the verdict cannot be sufficient without resolving the tension
  • A verdict leaving the team with no reviewer: the accountable owner is requested before it is communicated

Trade-offs

  • Stopping on sufficient evidence in exchange for incomplete coverage, declared in communicable limits
  • The base text advice "do not seek perfection" is replaced by the checkable condition "no open gap blocks the process"; the three-round cap moves from the prompt to the edge cases, where it still bounds the cycle with or without the owner sign-off, because the prompt budget went to the communicable limits. No step 4 instruction is lost

Assumptions

  • A previous team audit exists and new sources were imported into the shared base
  • The core "claims confirmed or refuted" is inherited from the standalone cross-check 04 and the sufficiency verdict from the standalone audit 05; here both apply to the delta of the shared base

Limits

  • It decides sufficiency over the set, it does not verify each claim in depth: that belongs to 04
  • It informs the owner review, it does not replace it, and it does not activate the conversational role: that belongs to W05

Acceptance criteria

  • The three roles behave differently and the difference shows in the first turn: explaining, recommending with operational risk, or making the user rephrase
  • Every turn carries a citation from the shared base or an explicit statement of limit
  • Any Notebook user can read the role limits without having attended the workshop

Edge cases

  • Question outside the shared base: the role states it and proposes a reviewable brief
  • Request for certainty the base does not hold: the available evidence and the remaining gap are shown

Trade-offs

  • A role bounded to the shared base in exchange for reliability towards any consulting user
  • This cell replaces the depth adjustment to the previous answer with the permanent visibility of the role limits: individual adaptation is lost and a role readable by anyone on the team is gained; no other step 5 instruction is lost

Assumptions

  • The shared base was declared sufficient in the previous step and several users will consult the same role
  • The mother rule of citing and splitting evidence, inference and missing data is inherited from the standalone coach 02; there the teaching flow is complete, here the activation is light

Limits

  • It activates a consultable role; it does not grade or compare individual performance: that belongs to W08
  • It does not design the persistent instruction or the team Notebook starter prompts: that belongs to W10

W05 · Printable work surfaces

W04 · Teacher / Advisor / Coach

RoleBehaviorQuestionOutputNo-go
TeacherExplains progressively and checks understandingWhat do you want to learn?Explanation + checkDo not advance without evidence of understanding
AdvisorCompares options, costs, risks and tensionsWhat decision must you make?Criteria-based recommendationDo not decide for the person
CoachAsks, reflects patterns and turns them into commitmentsWhat outcome and blocker do you have?Commitment + next stepDo not prescribe without context
02 · Deepening

Guided practice

Prompts 6–10 to create, apply, assess and rehearse from the sources.

Source rubric: coverage · authority · freshness · diversity · citations · sufficiency.

Insufficient: evidence is missing or weak sources dominate.

In progress: partial coverage and reviewable citations.

Sufficient: coverage, authority, freshness, diversity, citations and residual risk are explicit.

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every material claim is cited and inferences are labelled, so a reviewer can count them without opening the base
  • Each of the three editorial decisions names its type, its reason and its owner
  • Rights are reviewed before the piece is delivered

Edge cases

  • Commissioned thesis without support: the sustainable one is proposed and the operational risk is named
  • No owner assigned: it is requested before the package closes

Trade-offs

  • Reviewing rights and naming an owner adds friction in exchange for a piece defensible to third parties
  • The audience divergence is paid by compressing prose: the team cell keeps every instruction of the personal one and adds rights, operational risk and owner; no frozen instruction is dropped here

Assumptions

  • Someone is accountable for the piece and an editorial review happens after this step

Limits

  • It creates the piece; it neither publishes nor approves it: the review decides
  • It neither ranks a catalogue of use cases (W07) nor rehearses the defence to leadership (W09)

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Both scales are declared before scoring: value 1-5 by effect on the process and effort 1-5 by hours and complexity
  • Every ranked case carries cited support and an owner; cases without support appear marked speculative
  • The recommended experiment carries an observable metric, a threshold at seven days and a named operational risk

Edge cases

  • Base without process material: fewer than ten cases come out and the gap is declared
  • Experiment without an owner: it is requested before recommending it

Trade-offs

  • Fewer and more defensible cases: demanding cited support and an owner shrinks the catalogue in exchange for surviving review
  • The audience divergence is paid by compressing prose: the team cell keeps every instruction of the personal one and adds owner and operational risk; no frozen instruction disappears

Assumptions

  • Someone is accountable for each pilot and the ranking is reviewed afterwards

Limits

  • It estimates neither ROI nor prices, and does not replace the judgement of whoever decides the pilot
  • It ranks where to apply the base; it neither drafts the piece (W06) nor writes the final assistant instruction (W10)

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every answer gets one of the three rubric grades and the quote that justifies it
  • The close names the operational risk of enabling below the threshold declared by the process
  • Comparison runs across runs against the rubric; the result does not rank people

Edge cases

  • Foundations not demonstrated: the level repeats and the enabling risk is declared
  • Question without coverage: it is replaced and declared

Trade-offs

  • Less depth than the reusable assessor in exchange for a short workshop session tied to the Notebook
  • Receipt for the reframed token: the frozen text asked to «explain»; here it is preserved as a quoted correction, not as teaching; the audience divergence is paid by compressing prose and adding threshold, operational risk and comparability, without dropping frozen instructions

Assumptions

  • The process has an enabling threshold and an accountable owner who decides

Limits

  • It measures inside the workshop; the reusable instrument with its own rubric is 08
  • It does not teach the team: that is the coach activation W05
  • It informs enabling; it neither grants it nor ranks people

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The starter prompts are exactly 10, cover what the team asks first and none repeats another
  • The test guide can be run by anyone on the team and includes an out-of-base question that passes only if the assistant declares the limit
  • The instruction is ratified by the accountable owner before use, with limits coherent with the verdict already issued

Edge cases

  • Constraints against purpose: it stops before writing the instruction
  • No owner to ratify: one is requested before closing

Trade-offs

  • A conservative configuration in exchange for less apparent reach: the assistant promises what the base supports
  • The audience divergence is paid by compressing prose: the team cell keeps the instructions of the personal one and adds user per role, ratification and a test anyone can run; the non-exposure limit lives in guardrails and edge cases in both audiences, with no regression between them

Assumptions

  • The process declared the base sufficient and an accountable owner ratifies the instruction

Limits

  • It configures the assistant; it neither re-audits sources nor issues a sufficiency verdict: that closed in earlier workshop steps; from 07 the recommended configuration arrives, not the final instruction
  • It does not rank which cases are worth covering: that is W07
  • It authorizes neither publication nor connectors: owner ratification is a separate gate

P10 gate: purpose, two decisive sources, one accepted gap and a BASE SUFFICIENT or REPEAT RESEARCH verdict.

03 · Consolidation

Transfer and decide

Consolidate with evidence and your own explanation.

Independent challenge

Create a Notebook for a real decision, run steps 1–5 and use one deepening prompt. Deliver a source map, a sufficiency verdict and a three-minute explanation.

Teach-back: explain the method in 3 minutes. Second context: repeat it for another decision. Continuity: schedule a review in 7 days.

Complete

Complete: reviewable evidence exists.

Pending

Pending: the next action is clear.

coverage_gap

coverage_gap: a source, context or test is missing.

05 · Learn · Apprehend · Evolve

Choose your route

Estimated times. They vary with your iterations.

01≈ 30 min

Essential practice

Five steps to learn how to learn and configure your Notebook.

021–2 h

10-step route

Deepen, create, assess, simulate and configure through iterations.

032–4 h

Extended route

Turn reviewed research into a skill and test a local MCP connection.

01

Useful assistants

In 2026 assistants coexist with more autonomous agents. They remain useful for a clear function, stable instructions, fast creation, and controllable token use. They do not replace judgment or turn weak sources into evidence.

02

Reusable skills

A skill is a reusable package of instructions, criteria, resources, and checks that teaches an AI how to execute a task consistently. It must declare sources, limits, inputs, outputs, and tests.

Expert route · Spec → Build → Verify

Research to skill

  1. 01

    Define the skill decision and user.

  2. 02

    Use Research Blueprint to scope questions, sources, and acceptance.

  3. 03

    Run Deep Research and retain report, sources, and date.

  4. 04

    Audit authority, coverage, tensions, rights, and gaps.

  5. 05

    Import only approved sources into the open notebook or your own.

  6. 06

    Configure the Notebook as a source-grounded advisor and inspect citations.

  7. 07

    Write the skill contract: trigger, inputs, outputs, limits, and no-go.

  8. 08

    Ask the AI to create the skill from research without copying private data.

  9. 09

    Optionally configure a community local NotebookLM MCP; sign in yourself, review permissions, and avoid sensitive information.

  10. 10

    Run positive and adversarial cases; fix until sources, outputs, and limits are verifiable.

Optional setup

Google offers Antigravity IDE for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Its official guide requires Chrome and a personal Gmail account. Install from the official source, use review-driven development, and confirm current plan limits.

AntigravityGoogle Codelab

NotebookLM MCP

NotebookLM MCP is a community integration, not an official Google connector. It may automate a browser and retain a local session. Review the repository, pin a version, sign in personally, and avoid confidential sources.
